root_cause.text: In OCFS2’s freefrag ioctl path, `ocfs2_info_freefrag_scan_chain()` trusted the on-disk `bg_bits` field from a group descriptor as the bitmap scan bound, but the `OCFS2_INFO_FL_NON_COHERENT` path reads raw blocks via `ocfs2_read_blocks_sync()` without descriptor validation, allowing a crafted filesystem to make the bitmap walk run past the end of the group bitmap buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says “ocfs2_info_freefrag_scan_chain() uses on-disk bg_bits directly as the bitmap scan limit” and that the non-coherent path “uses ocfs2_read_blocks_sync() instead and skips that validation, so an impossible bg_bits value can drive the bitmap walk past the end of the block.” The patch adds `max_bitmap_bits = 8 * ocfs2_group_bitmap_size(...)` and clamps/report-logs when `bg_bits > max_bitmap_bits`, explicitly fixing the missing validation in `fs/ocfs2/ioctl.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Precompute the group bitmap bit limit in free-fragment scanning to ensure bitmap processing stays within valid bounds.
intent_record.what: The function `ocfs2_info_freefrag_scan_chain()` adds a new local variable `max_bitmap_bits` alongside `max_bits` and `num_clusters`, and initializes `max_bitmap_bits` before the main loop using `8 * ocfs2_group_bitmap_size(osb->sb, 0, osb->s_feature_incompat)`. No other lines in the shown hunk are changed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now has a precomputed upper bound for the number of bitmap bits available in a group descriptor. This value can be used to constrain later scanning logic so it does not process beyond the valid bitmap capacity, preventing out-of-range interpretation of free-space data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp invalid group descriptor bit counts during non-coherent freefrag scans to prevent out-of-bounds bitmap processing.
intent_record.what: The code adds a new check after reading `bg->bg_bits` in `ocfs2_info_freefrag_scan_chain()`: if `max_bits` is greater than `max_bitmap_bits`, it logs an error message and clamps `max_bits` down to `max_bitmap_bits` before continuing with the scan.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the free-space fragmentation scan from trusting an oversized group descriptor bit count when scanning raw blocks in non-coherent mode. It avoids iterating past the valid bitmap range and limits the scan to the maximum supported bitmap size, while emitting an error for the malformed descriptor.

candidates.rationale: This line trusts the on-disk group descriptor's bg_bits field as the upper bound for bitmap scanning. In the non-coherent path, the descriptor is read without validation, so a crafted filesystem can provide an invalid value and drive the bitmap walk past the buffer end.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the on-disk group descriptor field bg_bits as the upper bound for freefrag bitmap scanning. In the OCFS2 non-coherent ioctl path, the descriptor is read from raw blocks without validation, so a crafted filesystem can set an invalid bg_bits value and make the bitmap walk read past the end of the group bitmap buffer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in this snippet and the fix is not present. In `ocfs2_info_freefrag_scan_chain()` the code sets `max_bits = le16_to_cpu(bg->bg_bits);` and then walks the bitmap using `ocfs2_test_bit(offset, (unsigned long *)bg->bg_bitmap);` with the only bound check being `if ((offset + ffg->iff_chunksize) > max_bits) num_clusters = max_bits - offset;`. This shows the scan bound is taken directly from the on-disk `bg_bits` field. The non-coherent path is also present: `else status = ocfs2_read_blocks_sync(osb, blkno, 1, &bh);`, which reads raw blocks instead of validated descriptors. There is no validation of the group descriptor before using `bg_bits`/`bg_bitmap` in the non-coherent path, and no fix such as clamping against the actual bitmap buffer size or rejecting malformed descriptors.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `ocfs2_get_request_ptr()` only computes a user-pointer array base and copies out one request pointer: `bp = ...`, then `if (o2info_from_user(*req_addr, bp + idx)) goto bail;`. It does not contain the OCFS2 freefrag ioctl chain-scan logic, does not read `bg_bits`, and does not call `ocfs2_read_blocks_sync()` or any bitmap-walk code. Therefore the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent from this function. Because the bug is not present here, there is also no fix to detect in this snippet.
